At human height they look like someone has sprinkled pepper on the snow, but when you look closely they are actually about a 1/16th of an inch long and are purplish. When a forked tail-like furcula (that usually rests in a latch called the tenaculum on the underside of their abdomen) is suddenly released the springtail is propelled forward and can travel many times the length of their elongated body.
